## Design

### 2026-10-29: This entry is a combination of 2 days, because yesterday my entry didnt get uploaded. 1 hour 15 mins is backed by lapse, but for the rest then i forgot to unpause after i took a break.

**3.78h**

This entry is a combination of 2 days, because yesterday my entry didnt get uploaded. 1 hour 15 mins is backed by lapse, but for the rest then i forgot to unpause after i took a break.
i started by planning the entire project, deciding the specs and which ics to use. one big decision i had to make was whether to use rgb or monochromatic LEDs, and i decided to go with monochromatic, because for this project i feel rgb is not worth the hassle. i decided on the tpic6c595 shift register for the rows, and 74hct595 for the columns, using a common cathode. also a 74hct125 to bring up the 3.3v from the pico to 5v for the registers, and to maintain uniform voltage across multiple boards if they are connected together.
once all the decisions had been made and i had a plan in mind, i started with the schematic. i had to create my own symbols for the tpic6c595 and the 74hct125 as i couldnt find them in the symbol library.it wos my first time creating my own symbols and i made some basic mistakes which i rectified later on. once that was done, i studied each datasheet and made the connections between the chips and the led matrix. i recently learned about net lables, and using them has made my schematic much cleaner than it would have been. ive pretty much completed the schematic, unless i need to make changes later on.

### 2026-10-30: today i finished routing the pcb in one sitting- it took 3 hours. i started by assigning the footprints, and then arranging the components, which took quite a while. then i added some design rules(did

**3.15h**

today i finished routing the pcb in one sitting- it took 3 hours. i started by assigning the footprints, and then arranging the components, which took quite a while. then i added some design rules(didnt forget this time), and started routing. led matrices are really annoying to route, but it wasnt that bad. im gonna start with the firmware next time, and then if i have enough time, i might design an enclosure - though thatd have to be scalable too, so it might get a bit tough.

### 2026-11-01: this was the last stretch, i finished the code(logged that separately via hackatime), and made the repo. i explained the entire process of multiplexing and shift registers in the readme. i spent alot

**1.5h**

this was the last stretch, i finished the code(logged that separately via hackatime), and made the repo. i explained the entire process of multiplexing and shift registers in the readme. i spent alot of time finding the right components, because the TPIC6B595 chip just went out of stock, but thankfully i found a similar replacement. while adding the products to cart, i realised i used a 0603 footprint for a 100uf electrolytic capacitor, which would have caused big problems later, so im lucky i caught it now. the footprint size tripled so i had to move some things around and reroute some parts, but its all good now.
